metadata.title: Fed likely to 'stay put' on rates in 2026 after hot inflation data

content.text:
Coming off of May's hot Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) reading, Gradient Investments associate portfolio manager Lisa Schreiber weighs in on how the Federal Reserve may move on interest rates in 2026 based on the latest inflation data.
For more on the latest market action, we have Lisa Schreiber, Gradient Investments associate portfolio manager. Lisa, it's good to see you. So maybe start with the economic news today, Lisa. You know, we did get PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, rose 4.1% from a year earlier. That was the most since April 2023. Um, you know, listen, also, obviously old data and and oil has has pulled in hard here, Lisa, but curious to to get your take on it. What do you make of it? What do you think the Fed makes of it?
Yeah, very much uh interesting uh Josh for sure. I mean, the PC, that's uh obviously what the Fed um looks closes to. Um it came in um a little bit higher on on the headline, but at least in line on core PCE, what the Fed usually tends to look at stripping out volatile energy and and food prices. Um we're still very much above that two uh 2% target they have. And I think it was interesting when we uh had the FOMC meeting last uh week, which was also the first one of new chairman uh Kevin Warsh, that we have um that the um expectations or the bias towards a cut was stripped and uh exchanged for a bias towards a potential rate hike. So that was certainly very interesting. But I think overall, um the core uh numbers coming in in line could put investors a little bit to ease today and we saw it in the market actions today.
What is your base case for the Fed, Lisa? You think they stay put or no a hike could be coming before year end? What do you tell clients?
Well, expectations market is pricing in two to three rate hikes by now. We are not quite there yet. Um we think the Fed will stay put for the rest of the year. I think overall, um when we see um inflation pressures overall still still very much there, uh but again, when we look at Iran on all the oil prices and debt elevations and debt pressures to inflation, um we can still see a little bit more um movement towards a resolvement there. Um again, I will take a couple of months until that goes back to normal, but that certainly can put an ease to inflationary pressures, which we think will happen and will make at least uh the Fed stay put and not uh needing to hike rates.
Alicia, you mentioned Kevin stepping up to the mic for the first time there as chairman. What what did you make of of that press release? So what did you make of his tone, his style, how he was different than than Powell? Did did you appreciate the brief statement, Lisa?
Um definitely so, Josh. I mean, it was obviously heavily scrutinized because it was his first. The interesting thing is that he stayed away from giving economic guidance, what the Fed usually does. And um expectations are now that with all of these changes that he brings, that the Fed might uh strip out uh economic guidance at all going forward. That's that's certainly uh something we closely watch, but the brief statement obviously uh much more focused on on on the real numbers. That's certainly a plus um what we think here.
Well, let's talk about the great AI trade and trend, Lisa. You know, there there may have been some concern about uh the AI spending boom faltering, but, you know, listen, Micron reported, knocked it out of the park, that stock ripped higher in today's trade. What do you make of it?
Well, there was a lot going on lately with semis, right? I mean, running a little bit ahead of themselves. We had some chitters there. Micron put that um concern very much to the ease to your point. But again, like as markets really uh rally based on the AI and all of that $700 billion uh spending that is put to the ground to build out that. I mean investors are getting chish, right? And we saw that in other areas of the AI trade earlier this year. uh just reminding you of the Sesscapocalypse uh in software uh earlier this year. So there's certainly more volatility and these swings get a little bit higher from here, but there's certainly a lot of tailwind still in the market that we are seeing that this can continue but a little bit more volatility to be aware of for sure.
Let's end on some picks, Lisa, some names. Why is Rockwell Automation a buy?
Well, you just talked uh to your uh your guests before about warehouse um automation and all of that. And Rockwell Automation is really a leader and and try to um expand their manufacturing capabilities in all things uh packaging, uh warehouse robots and all of that. And um AI is certainly a very much uh tailwind for them because it increases their efficiency and how their systems work together and how that all is more efficient um in uh working within uh within a production company. So that is certainly a positive here and it's just another way to participate in the AI trade without being exposed to the names most on the forefront. I mean on a valuation perspective, it's not the cheapest, but I think there's a lot of momentum going on that can continue for the foreseeable future.
How about Chevron? Why why do I want that name in in my portfolio, Lisa?
Well, Chevron just um announced a 20-year deal with Microsoft empowering uh their data centers with natural gas. And I think Chevron is really one of the largest um uh energy companies over there and uh still um very much well set up to take on those deals. And um so again, it's another another interesting area to being participating in the AI trade without uh the most uh most known names there. Um it's still very uh very reasonable on a valuation's perspective. We can enjoy an over 4% dividend yield. And again, uh certainly for the stock or higher oil prices was a tailwind, um uh but that certainly um can continue to be a strain as oil prices are are hovering around higher elevated levels as still the Middle East tensions are going on.
And Lisa, finally your CRH. Now, that stock is down about 10% this year. Describe what they do and why you're a fan.
Well, CRH is a cement company, so nothing too exciting there on the first look, right? Uh but again, when we think of all the AI built out and all the data centers, well, what do we need to put all of these to the ground? A lot of cement. And CRH is really one of the leaders in North America to being provide uh to being able to provide that. Um so that is certainly a great tailwind for CRH. Uh they just um announced an uh a merger that should um expand their pipeline and their uh their their uh their um yeah, um increases even more. And also they are very well diversified between again, uh industrial data centers, all things roads and all of that, but also in the uh residential area. Um again, valuation it trades cheaper than the market and I think there's a lot um uh to being participating within the AI trade, um without being exposed to the most uh hot names out there. And it's really the picks and shovels quite literally of the AI trade.
Yeah, it has a lot of fans. about 90% of analysts on Wall Street say it's a buy, zero sells on that name. All right, Lisa, thanks as always for your time and picks. Appreciate it.
Thank you.
